cases.scope: Candidate1042 (confirmed runtime): emily (client) native swimming state22 and chain climbing state23 presented on the host remote emily body with bank70 in Edge of the World; swim 201/213 samples swimWeight>0.5, stroke 88, dive 22, surface 20; climb 163/224 samples climbWeight>0.5, ascend 117, descend 46, 51 cycle phases. Role parity, Emily (client) as source, both modes. Host observer camera video shows remote Emily grab the chain, climb up and down, release and land (sheet inspected). Swim video framed open sea (dock vantage faced away from the lane); swimming numeric only.

findings: Confirmed runtime: native swimming eye sits at the waterline (root ~-2.0, view ~-0.1, surface ~0 in native1035), so the faithfully placed remote body is mostly submerged; it is visible from a steep overhead view, not from dock level.
Confirmed runtime: presentation is role-symmetric; the Emily bank70 on the host and Corvo bank70 on the client both drive swim/climb layers from the same protocol72 states.
Harness: Set-ObserverPitch + immediate coop_observer_camera hold after an elevated setviewpos gives a stable overhead vantage (falls ~0.3 m before the hold).
outstanding: Swim mantle/water exit (no native exit state bound yet), underwater-only acting.
Chain hand-over-hand acting and grab/release transitions (clips 367/368 reserved); true ladders and top exits in other maps.
Polish (head height at the waterline, stroke cadence vs native speed ~3.5 m/s) deferred to the animator; editable sources kept.
